name: Groups Recover Together
one_liner: Buprenorphine (Suboxone) for opioid use with a weekly counselor-led group, in person or by video, in 13 states; takes Medicaid.

short_description: Suboxone plus a weekly counselor-led recovery group, in person or virtual, in 13 states; Medicaid, insurance or about $50–$65/week self-pay.
long_description: Groups Recover Together (Groups, run by Recover Together, Inc., founded in 2014) is an outpatient opioid treatment provider. Members get buprenorphine (Suboxone) from a medical provider, usually by video, and attend a one-hour weekly group led by a licensed counselor, held at local offices or online, plus practical recovery support. Groups says it serves 13 states and can treat people outside its office locations virtually within those states. It accepts Medicaid and many commercial plans. For uninsured patients without financial help, its April 2025 policy sets a weekly fee ($50 a week in Maine and New Hampshire); another Groups page lists $65 a week. There is an app for scheduling and joining groups. Group-based buprenorphine care is an established model, but no published study of Groups' own outcomes was found.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance or Medicaid; $50/week self-pay (Maine and New Hampshire)
pricing.notes: April 2025 self-pay policy: weekly fee for uninsured patients without approved financial assistance ($50/week, or every other week in step-down, in ME and NH). Another Groups page lists $65/week. State grant programs may cover uninsured patients. Medication billed separately.

privacy.notes: Treatment records are covered by its HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 notice (May 2026); the website policy found did not say whether data is sold or shared for advertising.

seo.meta_description: Groups Recover Together provides office-based and virtual group therapy combined with Suboxone treatment for opioid addiction, with peer support at the core.

faqs.q: How does group treatment work at GRT?
faqs.a: Weekly group sessions combine check-ins, skill building, and peer support with 8-12 members. A licensed counselor facilitates each group. Medical appointments for Suboxone prescribing happen separately with a provider. Most find the community aspect crucial to their recovery.

faqs.q: How much does Groups Recover Together cost?
faqs.a: GRT accepts most insurance including Medicaid, often with low or no copays. Self-pay options exist where needed. The group model keeps costs manageable compared to individual therapy-only approaches.

faqs.q: Can I do virtual groups with GRT?
faqs.a: Yes, GRT offers both in-person and virtual group options in most locations. Virtual groups provide flexibility while maintaining the peer support element. Some patients combine virtual and in-person attendance.

faqs.q: Is group treatment effective for opioid addiction?
faqs.a: Research shows group therapy combined with MAT has strong outcomes. The peer support component helps with accountability and reduces isolation common in addiction. Many prefer groups to individual treatment for the community aspect.

primary_uses: Buprenorphine (Suboxone) treatment for opioid use disorder

patient_summary: You do an intake, then see a prescriber (usually by video) for buprenorphine (Suboxone) and join a one-hour weekly group led by a licensed counselor, in person or online. Groups takes Medicaid and many insurance plans; if you're uninsured, there is a weekly self-pay fee ($50/week in Maine and New Hampshire) and some states have grants.

availability.note: 13 US states, in person at local offices or virtually within those states.
